title: Costs, break-even and depreciation
subtitle: Which costs change with the decision, where revenue overtakes cost, and how an asset’s value is spread over its life.

kinds.title: Kinds of cost
kinds.body: Fixed costs do not change with output (rent, insurance); variable costs do (materials, energy). Direct costs trace to a product, indirect (overhead) do not. A sunk cost is already spent and irrecoverable — it must be ignored in a forward-looking decision. Marginal cost is the cost of one more unit.

total.title: Total, average and marginal cost
total.body: Total cost TC = FC + VC. Average cost AC = TC/Q falls while marginal cost MC is below it and rises when MC is above it — so MC cuts AC at its minimum (the efficient scale). With FC = 120,000 and variable cost Rs 30 per unit, AC at 4,000 units is 30 + 120,000/4,000 = 60.

bep.title: Break-even analysis
bep.body: Revenue = price × quantity; break-even is where revenue equals total cost: Q* = FC/(p − v), the fixed cost divided by the contribution margin per unit. Selling price Rs 50, variable cost Rs 30, FC Rs 120,000: Q* = 120,000/20 = 6,000 units. Above it profit is (p − v)(Q − Q*).
bep.steps: Contribution margin per unit. Break-even quantity.

dep.title: Depreciation: why and what
dep.body: An asset loses value with use and time. Depreciation allocates its cost over its life as an expense (it is not a cash outflow — the cash went out when it was bought). Book value = cost − accumulated depreciation; it never drops below salvage value. Depreciation matters for money because it is tax-deductible.

sl.title: Straight-line method
sl.body: D = (P − S)/N each year. For P = Rs 100,000, S = Rs 10,000, N = 5: D = 18,000 per year, book value falling by the same step.

ddb.title: Declining-balance and MACRS
ddb.body: Double declining balance takes a fixed fraction 2/N of the remaining book value each year (ignoring salvage until the end, never going below it): bigger deductions early. Same asset: year 1 40,000, year 2 24,000, year 3 14,400, year 4 8,640, year 5 2,960. MACRS (used for tax in the USA) assigns standard percentage tables per asset class.
ddb.steps: Rate = 2/N = 2/5 = 40 %. Year 1 on Rs 100,000. Depreciation then = 40,000; book value 60,000. Year 2 = 40 % of 60,000 = 24,000.

tax.title: Income taxes in decisions
tax.body: Taxable income = revenue − operating cost − depreciation. Tax = rate × taxable income. After-tax cash flow = (revenue − cost) − tax. Depreciation lowers tax, creating a tax shield of rate × D each year.
tax.steps: Revenue 80,000, cash costs 30,000, depreciation 18,000, tax rate 30 %. Taxable = 32,000; tax = 9,600; after-tax cash flow = 50,000 − 9,600.
